split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Baseline. Validation ROC-AUC 0.8196, best epoch 7 of 13. Without class weights the recall at the 0.5 cut-off is only 0.16 (precision 0.61).

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Wider and deeper: ROC-AUC 0.8190 (-0.0006 vs D01) with 16 epochs. Training AUC is +0.003 above validation at the best epoch, the largest gap of the runs, a hint of overfitting but no gain.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Single hidden layer of 32: ROC-AUC 0.8191 (-0.0005 vs D01). A much smaller network scores about the same, so network size is not what limits the result; it needed 22 epochs to reach its best.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Dropout 0.3: ROC-AUC 0.8199 (+0.0003 vs D01, within noise). Training is slower (best epoch 25) and recall at the 0.5 cut-off drops to 0.12.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Batch normalization: ROC-AUC 0.8181 (-0.0015 vs D01); training stopped after 12 epochs. No benefit on this small network.

single_change: Optimizer SGD with momentum, learning rate 0.01
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: SGD with momentum (learning rate 0.01): ROC-AUC 0.8191. It needed 20 epochs to reach its best against 7 for Adam, so it converges more slowly for the same quality.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: RMSprop: ROC-AUC 0.8195, PR-AUC 0.4454. Very close to Adam (D01).

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Adam with a 10 times larger learning rate (0.01): ROC-AUC 0.8193. Training did not become unstable here (ReduceLROnPlateau can halve the rate when progress stalls, which may hide an unstable start).

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Adam with a 10 times smaller learning rate (0.0001): ROC-AUC 0.8189. Best epoch 40 of 40 (the limit is 40), so it was still improving when it was stopped and is probably not fully trained.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Class weights: ROC-AUC 0.8195 (same ranking quality as D01) but recall 0.79 against 0.16, precision 0.32 against 0.61, accuracy 0.707. Class weights change the balance of errors, not how well people are ranked.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Dropout 0.3 + class weights: ROC-AUC 0.8195, recall 0.81, precision 0.31. Compare with D04 (dropout only) and D10 (class weights only).

model: Neural net 64-32, mean of 5 random starts
single_change: Repeat with 5 random starts (measures the noise)
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Same network with 5 random starts: ROC-AUC 0.8192 +/- 0.0006 (std), range 0.8186 to 0.8202. Noise from the starting weights alone is about 0.0012 (2 std).

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Accuracy 0.847 only because it answers 'no diabetes' for everyone: recall 0, F1 0, ROC-AUC 0.50. Shows that accuracy is misleading on this data.

single_change: First real model: logistic regression with class weights
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Class-weighted linear model: ROC-AUC 0.815, recall 0.77 but precision only 0.32. Trains in 0.4 s. A strong, cheap reference point.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Unlimited-depth forest: ROC-AUC 0.779 and recall only 0.16 at the 0.5 cut-off. AUC rose from 0.735 (10 trees) to 0.776 (100) and 0.779 (200), so more trees help little. Tuning (T07) fixed most of the gap with shallower trees.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Default boosting is already the best untuned model: ROC-AUC 0.820, PR-AUC 0.445, in 2.6 s.

single_change: Different model family: SVM (20,000-row training sample)
features: 25 features (21 original + 4 engineered), trained on 20,000-row sample
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: SVM trained on 20,000 rows (about 12% of the training set): ROC-AUC 0.800. Not a fair comparison with the full-data models, and the cost of the SVM grows quickly with more rows.

single_change: Tune C and class weighting (grid search, 3-fold CV)
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Tuning changed nothing: C from 0.01 to 10 and class weighting gave CV ROC-AUC between 0.8084 and 0.8086. The limit comes from the linear form of the model, not from the regularisation.

single_change: Tune depth, leaf size and max_features (random search, 3-fold CV)
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Best settings: max_depth 12, min_samples_leaf 50, max_features 0.5. ROC-AUC rose from 0.779 (T03) to 0.817 and F1 0.460 is the highest F1 of all runs. Shallower, smoother trees reduced the overfitting of T03.

single_change: Tune learning rate, leaves, leaf size and L2 (random search, 3-fold CV)
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Best traditional model: learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 15, min_samples_leaf 20, l2 10. ROC-AUC 0.8199, PR-AUC 0.4457. Gain over the default T04 is only 0.0002 in AUC, so tuning barely mattered.

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Same model without the 4 engineered features: ROC-AUC 0.8195 vs 0.8199 and PR-AUC 0.4455 vs 0.4457. No measurable benefit from the new features on this split (run-to-run variation was not measured).

split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: Without class weights the ranking quality is the same (ROC-AUC 0.8200), but recall falls from 0.79 to 0.17 while precision rises from 0.32 to 0.58 and accuracy to 0.855. Class weights change the balance of errors at the 0.5 cut-off, not how well people are ranked.

features: 25 features (21 original + 4 engineered), SMOTE on train
split: stratified 70/15/15, seed 42, duplicates removed (train 160,631 / val 34,421 / test 34,422)
observations: SMOTE (training set only): ROC-AUC 0.818, recall 0.25, precision 0.54. It moves the balance of errors less than class weights and the AUC is slightly lower than T08.

single_change: Repeat on 5 random splits (measures the noise)
split: 5 random stratified 70/15/15 splits (seeds 1 to 5), duplicates removed
observations: Same model on 5 random splits: ROC-AUC 0.8178 +/- 0.0017 (std), range 0.8158 to 0.8199. Differences below about 0.0034 between experiments are within the split noise.
